text:
maya: Quick heads-up — after the midnight deploy I'm seeing p99 latency regressions on small interactive requests. root cause looks like the selector prefers the `vectorized_fast` kernel for seq<=16 and small batches, but its per-call launch cost is killing us when continuous batching doesn't merge requests.
liam: ugh, saw a blip in staging too. can you drop the pprof/flamegraph? :eyes:
maya: pasted top lines from flamegraph dump below (kept short):
```
45%  kernel_launch
20%  vectorized_fast_infer
10%  kv_cache_lookup
8%   scheduler_coalesce_wait
7%   fallback_path_sync
```
maya: metrics: small-req cohort (seq<=16, bs<=6) p99 went 48ms -> 120ms. throughput unaffected for large batches.
ops-bot: deploy v2026.03.18-3 finished on g5x-pool :white_check_mark:
ana: quick q — is this purely launch overhead or contention with KV warmups?
maya: looks both. KV hits are fine after first token, but for tiny requests the selector chooses vectorized_fast which needs a fresh kernel handshake that stalls while KV frames warm. combined cost ~50-70ms.
liam: could we bias selector to prefer `compact_path` for <8 tokens? That path has slightly slower per-token but much smaller launch setup.
nana: I prototyped a tweak — lower score for vectorized_fast when batch_size<=8 or seq_len<=20. config snippet: 
```json
{"selector": {"rules": [ {"match": {"seq_le": 20, "batch_le": 8}, "prefer": "compact_path", "score_delta": -15} ]}}
```
ravi: also think about scheduler side — our continuous-batching window is 4ms. microbursts at client side produce many small batches that never merge. increasing coalesce window to 8ms might let batching absorb launch cost without hurting latency much.
maya: ran an A/B on staging: coalesce:4ms + selector tweak = p99 55ms; coalesce:8ms + selector tweak = p99 40ms. undoing selector only gave 85ms.
perf-bot: perf alert: small-req-p99 exceeded threshold at 2312349800. linked dashboard: https://perf.redwood.local/d/small-reqs
liam: nice numbers. risks of raising coalesce window? tail latency for slightly longer requests?
nana: risk small. we should run real-traffic shadow for 30m. also need a regression test in CI that simulates sparse microburst traffic shapes.
ravi: logging note — selector emits `chosen_kernel` but not seq/batch metadata. add fields `chosen_kernel_reason` and `batch_shape` to traces so we can debug later.
maya: filed infra ticket and will roll the selector rule to canary. plan: revert to previous selector if p99>90ms on canary. @ravi can you add trace fields?
ravi: on it, will push small tracing patch in 10m.
liam: once traces are in, I can run a deeper pprof to confirm handshake path. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
maya: thanks — tracking in #eng-runtime and will post canary results.
